first-controller.title: Create Your First Controller
first-controller.description: Learn the basics of creating api-ape controllers

steps.title: Understanding Controllers
steps.content: Controllers in api-ape are simple JavaScript files in your `api/` directory. Each exported function becomes an endpoint that clients can call.

steps.title: Create a Controller File
steps.description: Create a new file in your api/ directory

steps.title: Export a Function
steps.description: Export a function from your controller that returns a value

steps.title: Test Your Endpoint
steps.description: Call your endpoint from a client to verify it works

steps.title: Controller Created!
steps.content: Congratulations! You've created your first api-ape controller. Your endpoint is now available at `api.greet.yourFunction()`.

broadcast-master.title: Master Broadcasting
broadcast-master.description: Learn to broadcast messages to all connected clients

steps.title: What is Broadcasting?
steps.content: Broadcasting sends a message to ALL connected clients simultaneously. This is useful for real-time updates like notifications, chat messages, or live data feeds.

steps.title: Broadcast to Others
steps.content: Use `this.broadcastOthers()` to send to all clients EXCEPT the caller. Perfect for chat apps where the sender already knows their own message.

steps.title: Create a Broadcast Endpoint
steps.description: Create a controller that uses this.broadcast() to send a message to all clients
steps.hint: Create a function that calls this.broadcast({...})

steps.title: Test Your Broadcast
steps.description: Open two browser tabs and verify both receive the broadcast
steps.hint: Call your broadcast endpoint from one tab and see the message in both

steps.title: Broadcast Master!
steps.content: You've mastered broadcasting! You can now send real-time updates to all connected clients.

steps.title: What is Pub/Sub?
steps.content: Pub/Sub (Publish/Subscribe) lets you subscribe to specific channels and receive messages published to them. Unlike broadcasting, you only receive messages from channels you're subscribed to.

steps.title: Subscription Syntax
steps.content: Use `api.subscribe.channel.name(callback)` to subscribe. The channel name can be any path - it's automatically created when you subscribe.

steps.title: Create a Subscription
steps.description: Subscribe to a channel in your client code

steps.title: Publish a Message
steps.content: On the server, use `this.publish.channel.name(data)` or `ape.publish.channel.name(data)` to send messages to subscribers.

steps.title: First Subscriber!
steps.content: You've learned pub/sub messaging! Use subscriptions for targeted real-time updates.

basic-auth.title: Implement Basic Authentication
basic-auth.description: Secure your endpoints with Tier 1 authentication

steps.title: Authentication Tiers
steps.content:
api-ape supports 4 authentication tiers:

- **Tier 0 (Guest)**: No authentication
- **Tier 1 (Basic)**: OPAQUE/PAKE or SSO
- **Tier 2 (Elevated)**: Tier 1 + MFA
- **Tier 3 (High Security)**: 2-of-3 Shamir Secret Sharing

steps.title: Set Up Auth Framework
steps.content: Configure the authentication framework with OPAQUE (password-authenticated key exchange) where the server never sees the raw password.

steps.title: Protect an Endpoint
steps.description: Add authentication checking to a controller endpoint

steps.title: Tier 1 Secured!
steps.content: Your endpoints are now protected with basic authentication. Next step: add MFA for Tier 2!

steps.title: What are Lifecycle Hooks?
steps.content: Lifecycle hooks let you run code at key moments: when clients connect, disconnect, send messages, or receive responses.

steps.title: onConnect Hook
steps.content:
The `onConnect` hook fires when a client establishes a WebSocket connection. Use it to:
- Validate connections
- Attach custom data to the socket
- Send welcome messages

steps.title: Implement a Hook
steps.description: Add an onConnect or onDisconnect hook to your server
steps.hint: Add the hook in your ape() configuration

steps.title: Hook Master!
steps.content: You've mastered lifecycle hooks. Use them to control every aspect of client connections.

file-upload.title: Upload Your First File
file-upload.description: Learn binary file transfers with api-ape

steps.title: Binary File Transfers
steps.content: api-ape supports efficient binary file uploads over WebSocket. Files are streamed in chunks, making it memory-efficient for large files.

steps.title: Server-Side Handler
steps.content: On the server, binary data arrives as ArrayBuffer. You can save it to disk or process it.

steps.title: Implement File Upload
steps.description: Create a file upload endpoint and client code

steps.title: File Uploader!
steps.content: You can now handle binary file uploads. Next: try downloading files!
